claim_findings.passage: Management still frames roughly $40 billion as the relevant buyback capacity, now expecting it can actually be deployed over time, with a target of deploying capital at a 17% return.
claim_findings.evidence: Read in full context (seg-0079), the $40 billion is excess capital, and Dimon's point is the opposite of buyback capacity. He says 'if we think we can deploy, it's very different than buying back stock', 'buying back stock is not returning money to shareholders. You're making an investment decision', and lists organic and inorganic uses. Labelling the number 'buyback capacity' and then saying it will be 'deployed' inverts the signal management gave.
claim_findings.recommendation: Restate claim_text as excess or deployable capital of approximately $40 billion that management now expects to deploy over time, rather than buyback capacity.

claim_findings.passage: Management describes a mild but broad-based loosening in competitors' credit underwriting standards
claim_findings.evidence: The claim's own quote says the opposite of broad-based: 'and this is not across the board, by the way. It's more some players than others.' In the segment, 'it's across several spectrum' means across several dimensions of underwriting, not across the market. claim_text is internally contradictory with the quote it carries.
claim_findings.recommendation: Replace 'broad-based' with wording that keeps the distinction: mild loosening across several dimensions of underwriting, concentrated in some lenders rather than market-wide.

claim_findings.passage: AWM reported net income of $2 billion with a 38% pre-tax margin; revenue of $6.9 billion was up 19% year-on-year; AUM of $5.1 trillion was up 18% year-on-year and client assets of $7.7 trillion were up 19% year-on-year.
claim_findings.evidence: The AUM and client-asset figures are not in this claim's quote, which stops at the revenue driver sentence. They are true (seg-0003 states them) but they are the content of claim-015's quote. The same pattern appears in claim-025 (the 30-40% job-reduction detail belongs to claim-026's quote), claim-027 (the delinquency and FICO detail is in seg-0076 but not in the quote), claim-038 (Equities up 45% and Banking up 34% are in web-004 but not in the quote) and claim-039 (the 12% dividend increase is in web-004 but not in the quote). Every instance checks out against its underlying source, so this is an auditability weakness, not a factual error: a reader auditing the claim from its own quote cannot confirm the extra assertion.
claim_findings.recommendation: Extend each quote to cover everything claim_text asserts, or move the extra assertion into the claim that already quotes it.

outlook_findings.evidence: Two problems in one clause. First, the citation is the wrong claim for the sentence: claim-009 is average deposit growth (3% year-on-year, 2% quarter-on-quarter), not CCB segment growth. The claim that reports CCB growth is claim-008. Second, the characterisation contradicts the only reported CCB figure: CCB revenue was up 8% year-on-year, which is not low-to-mid single digit. The base case therefore projects a CCB growth rate below what the quarter actually delivered, on a claim that does not measure it.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Cite claim-008 and describe CCB growth consistently with the reported 8%, or state explicitly that the base case assumes deceleration and say why.

outlook_findings.passage: and the broader risk-on market backdrop management describes [claim-011] persists longer than the "as good as it gets" framing offered in the call implies
outlook_findings.evidence: Two citation problems. claim-011 is about the investment-banking pipeline and deal conversion; it says nothing about a risk-on market backdrop. The claim that carries management's market-conditions language is claim-012 ('the highly dynamic market conditions'). Separately, the quoted phrase 'as good as it gets' is attributed to the call but appears in no claim: it comes from seg-0040 (Dimon: 'It's getting close to as good as it gets. We just don't know how long it's going to last') and seg-0060, neither of which was extracted. This repeats a lesson already recorded in .agents/memory/extractor-lessons.md about quoted phrases having to appear in the cited claim.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Cite claim-012 for the market backdrop, and either extract Dimon's 'as good as it gets' remark as a claim or drop the quotation.

outlook_findings.passage: Markets strength was uneven: Fixed Income grew a more modest 6%, while Equities grew 86%, driven by major IPOs, index rebalancing, unusually complex Korean equity market dynamics, and broad client activity across regions [claim-012][claim-033].
outlook_findings.evidence: Balance and use of available evidence. The brief's central judgment is that the Equities surge is the least repeatable part of the quarter. Validated peer claims in this run bear directly on that question and are never used: Citigroup's Equity markets revenue rose 45% (claim-038) and Bank of America's Equities revenue rose 70% (in web-002, extracted but not claimed). A market-wide equities surge is meaningfully different in forecasting terms from a JPM-specific one. The peer claims (claim-037 through claim-041) appear only in a passing aside in section 9 and are never brought to bear on the analysis they are most relevant to.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Use the peer claims where they matter: compare JPM's 86% Equities growth against the peers' own equities prints and say whether that strengthens or weakens the normalisation assumption in the base case.

outlook_findings.passage: AWM revenue up 19% with record AUM growth [claim-014]
outlook_findings.evidence: Nothing in claim-014, claim-015 or seg-0003 describes AUM growth as a record. The transcript says AUM of $5.1 trillion was up 18% year-on-year. 'Record' is an unsupported intensifier added by the brief.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Drop 'record' or replace with the stated 18% year-on-year AUM growth.

outlook_findings.passage: Buyback capacity remains framed at approximately \$40 billion, which management now believes it can actually deploy over time, against a stated target of deploying capital at a 17% return [claim-028][claim-029].
outlook_findings.evidence: This inherits the mischaracterisation in claim-028 (see that finding). In seg-0079 the $40 billion is excess capital and the thrust of the answer is that management expects to deploy it into growth rather than repurchase stock. As written, the brief reads as if a $40 billion buyback is the plan.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Reword to excess or deployable capital, and note management's explicit preference for deployment over repurchase.

summary: One high-severity finding blocks this run. outlook-brief.md section 9 states that Wells Fargo could not be cited because the only extracted page was an unlabeled chart image. That is false about this run's own evidence: web-003 is the full Wells Fargo press release in clean text, with net income, EPS, revenue, ROTCE and complete segment tables. The brief therefore reports a gap that does not exist and drops a peer on that basis. Four medium findings follow: claim-028 and section 3 recast Dimon's $40 billion of excess capital as buyback capacity when the point of his answer was that he expects to deploy it rather than repurchase stock; the base case describes CCB growth as low-to-mid single digit while citing the deposit-growth claim, when reported CCB revenue growth was 8%; the upside case cites the investment-banking pipeline claim for a market-backdrop statement and quotes 'as good as it gets' from the call although no claim contains it; and the validated peer claims are never brought to bear on the brief's central judgment that the 86% Equities surge is not repeatable, even though Citigroup's Equity markets revenue rose 45% and Bank of America's Equities revenue rose 70% in the same quarter. Lower-severity issues cover an unsupported 'record' intensifier and a recurring pattern of claim_text asserting figures that sit outside the claim's own quote. Deterministic gates all passed, the injection scan was clean, period labelling is unambiguous throughout, temporal integrity holds, and the prose is appropriately bank-specific.
proposed_lessons: Before writing in the brief that a source could not be used, re-open every archived evidence file for that entity, since a second capture of the same report is often cleanly extracted even when another is an unreadable chart deck.
Keep each claim's quote self-sufficient: if claim_text asserts a figure or qualifier, that figure or qualifier must appear in the claim's own quote, not merely elsewhere in the same segment or page.
When peer or competitor evidence is extracted, use it in the section whose judgment it actually bears on, rather than mentioning it only in the uncertainties section.
